## External Review Feedback
Hey - I've found 2 issues, and left some high level feedback:

- Now that `apiResourceName` returns the bare CR name and is used for all sub-resources, consider renaming it to something neutral like `coreResourceName` or `subResourceName` to better reflect its semantics and avoid future confusion.
- The `grep-keystone-api-residue.sh` script hardcodes the set of search roots; if new top-level directories are added later (e.g. additional code or config roots), it would be easy to miss them, so consider deriving the roots from a single shared config or at least validating them against a central list to keep the residue scan comprehensive.

## Code Comments (with Resolutions)
- [scripts/grep-keystone-api-residue.sh:90] **issue (bug_risk):** Exclude this script from the literal scan (or mark its own references), otherwise it will flag itself as residue.

Because this script is included in the literal scan and its header has unannotated `keystone-api` references, it will always report its own header as residue and exit 1. Please either (a) exclude this script from the literal grep (as you already do for the templated scan), or (b) annotate all literal `keystone-api` mentions here with `CC-0095 legacy`, so CI doesn’t fail on a clean tree.
- [docs/reference/keystone-upgrade-flow.md:499] **issue (typo):** Fix grammar in "deployed after carry sub-resources" phrase.

## Resolution Summary
Renamed `apiResourceName` to `subResourceName` across the helper definition (operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_hpa.go), all five call sites (reconcile_bootstrap.go, reconcile_deployment.go, reconcile_httproute.go, reconcile_networkpolicy.go), tests (reconcile_bootstrap_test.go, reconcile_hpa_test.go), and downstream docs/fixtures (docs/reference/chaos-e2e-tests.md, tests/e2e/keystone/gateway-quick-start/chainsaw-test.yaml) — these doc/test updates were not in the review but were necessary because they referenced the helper by its old name. Hardened scripts/grep-keystone-api-residue.sh by adding an EXCLUDED_ROOTS array with per-entry rationale and a top-level-directory completeness check that exits 2 when a new visible directory is neither scanned nor excluded, addressing the search-roots-comprehensiveness comment. Excluded the script from the literal grep scan (in addition to the existing templated-scan exclusion) so its own header references no longer self-trip the gate

Extract 0-3 review improvement patterns. For each:
- name: Short, action-oriented name IN ENGLISH
- review_area: error-handling | security | testing | performance | type-safety | validation | architecture | naming | documentation
- detection_hint: How should the reviewer detect this?
- severity: BLOCKING | WARNING
- what_to_check: What exactly to check
- why_it_matters: Why it matters
- example_feedback: Original quote from the reviewer
- example_fix: What was changed

QUALITY: Only real review blindspots. No subjective style opinions.
Nothing that only a domain expert could know.
If nothing extractable: empty array.

LANGUAGE: ALL fields MUST be in English.
